observation.visible_scene: A single circular, transparent, disk-shaped object (resembling an optical disc/CD) is held up against a pure black background and backlit, so its surface glows with concentric thin-film interference rings: a pale-yellow band near the top, then green, cyan and a wide deep-blue annulus, with a hint of magenta on the right edge. A central spindle hole appears as a black disc ringed by a bright reflective crescent (strongest at the bottom). On the left, a dark scalloped silhouette of fingers grips the rim of the disc, holding it steady in front of the light.
visible_changes: The iridescent color pattern shifts steadily across the disc during the excerpt: the yellow band at the top progressively narrows and is overtaken by cyan/green, and by the last frames the whole disc reads as predominantly deep blue/cyan rather than the yellow-topped pattern of the first frames.
The magenta/purple band on the right edge shrinks and fades toward cyan over the same interval.
The disc as a whole drifts slightly to the right (and marginally downward) within the frame from first to last view.
The central hole and its bright lower rim keep a constant position and shape relative to the colored rings, indicating one rigid object reorienting rather than parts moving independently.
The finger silhouette on the left remains in contact with the disc edge throughout, with no new grip or release visible inside the segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produces the color shift (the hand tilting/rotating the disc relative to an unseen light source) is not directly shown; only its optical consequence is visible.
The light source, the holder's body, and any motion before t=0 or after t=2.667 s are outside the crop.
Whether the disc is spinning in-plane or merely tilting about a horizontal axis cannot be resolved from the color motion alone.
uncertain_details: Because the background is featureless black, the slight rightward drift of the disc cannot be confidently attributed to object translation versus small camera movement.
The exact orientation/axis of the disc's reorientation is inferred from the moving color bands, not from a visible edge-on view.
The faint radial 'spoke' texture in the blue region may rotate, but the change is too subtle to confirm.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
